```{r local_func, include=FALSE}
interpret_rsqr <- function(rsqr) {
  if (rsqr < 0.01) {
    "Very little of the observed variation in the data can be   
    explained by the regression model. Historically, the regression has not performed   
    well at other gages with similar R-squared values."
    } else if (rsqr < 0.1) {
      "Little of the observed variation in the data can be 
      explained by the regression model. Historically, the regression has not consistenty
      performed well at other gages with similar R-squared values."
      } else if (rsqr < 0.2) {
        "Some of the observed variation in the data can be 
        explained by the regression model. Historically, the regression has performed 
        decently well at other gages with similar R-squared values."
        } else if (rsqr < 0.35) {
          "A considerable amount of the observed variation in the 
          data can be explained by the regression model. Historically, the regression has
          performed well at other gages with similar R-squared values."
          } else {
            "An exceptional amount of the observed variation in the
            data can be explained by the regression model (relative to other gages). 
            Historically, the regression has performed well at other gages with similar 
            R-squared values."
          }
}
```

```{r loop, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = TRUE}
  return_plotly = FALSE,
  include_days_before = 60,
  use_limits = TRUE
)
  
  forecast_plot[[as.character(sd)]] <- forecast_plot[[as.character(sd)]] +

      x = "Date",
      y = "Flow (cfs)",
      title = "Observed and Projected Flows"

# create forecast table
all_flow <- forecast_data %>%
  full_join(Constant_AGWRC, by = c("Day", "Date", "obs_flow" )) %>%
  full_join(Iterative_AGWRC, by = c("Day", "Date", "obs_flow" )) %>%
  full_join(Variable_AGWRC, by = c("Day", "Date", "obs_flow" ))

final_flow_df <- all_flow %>%
  select(Day, Date, obs_flow, Con_AGWRC_Flow, Var_AGWRC_Flow, Itr_AGWRC_Flow) %>%
  rename(Obs_Flow = obs_flow)

Forecast_df <- final_flow_df %>%
  filter(Day %in% c(15, 30, 45, 90)) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(Obs_Flow, Con_AGWRC_Flow, Var_AGWRC_Flow, Itr_AGWRC_Flow),
  ~ round(.x, params$digits)))

forecast_table[[as.character(sd)]] <- flextable(Forecast_df) %>%
  autofit()

}
```

```{r rating_class function, include = FALSE}
# function for determining AGWRC method based on the case study rating_class
  rating_class_method <- function(cs_rating_class) {
    if (cs_rating_class == 0 | cs_rating_class == 1 | cs_rating_class == 4) {
      method = "lm_variable"
    } else if (cs_rating_class == 2) {
      method = "lm_constant"
    } else if (cs_rating_class == 3) {
      method = BPJ_AGWRC
    } else if (cs_rating_class == 5 | cs_rating_class == 6 | cs_rating_class == 7) {
      message("No projection available")
      method <- NA
    }
    return(method)
  }
```

```{r QC metrics code, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#Query QC data from database
qc_data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  conn = ds$connection,
  paste0(
    "SELECT
     feat.name, feat.hydrocode, 
     props.propname, props.propvalue,
     props.propcode, slope.propvalue as watershed_slope
  FROM dh_feature as feat
  LEFT JOIN dh_properties as model
     ON model.featureid = feat.hydroid
     AND model.propcode = 'AGWRC-1.0'
  LEFT JOIN dh_properties as props
     ON props.featureid = model.pid
  LEFT JOIN dh_properties as slope
     ON slope.featureid = feat.hydroid
     AND slope.propname = 'wshd_slope'
  WHERE feat.bundle = 'watershed'
     AND feat.ftype = 'usgs_full_drainage'
     AND feat.hydrocode = '",
  gage_obj$gage_feature$hydrocode,"'"
  )
)

#Filter by propname to find only our QC fields
qc_df <- qc_data[qc_data$propname %in% c(
  "white_test_p",  "breusch_pagan_p",
  "non_na_flow_count", "total_bf_events",
  "jan_bf_events", "feb_bf_events", "mar_bf_events",
   "apr_bf_events", "may_bf_events", "jun_bf_events",   
   "jul_bf_events", "aug_bf_events", "sep_bf_events",       
   "oct_bf_events", "dec_bf_events", "nov_bf_events",       
   "regression_m", "regression_b", "regression_Rsq",      
   "regression_m_pvalue", "regression_b_pvalue"
),]

#Filter for monthly bf values
monthly_bf <- qc_df %>%
  filter(propname %in% c (
    "jan_bf_events", "feb_bf_events", "mar_bf_events",
   "apr_bf_events", "may_bf_events", "jun_bf_events",   
   "jul_bf_events", "aug_bf_events", "sep_bf_events",       
   "oct_bf_events", "nov_bf_events", "dec_bf_events"
  ))

#Remove unwanted columns

#Rename values
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "jan_bf_events"] <- "January"

monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "apr_bf_events"] <- "April"

monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "jun_bf_events"] <- "June"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "jul_bf_events"] <- "July"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "aug_bf_events"] <- "August"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "sep_bf_events"] <- "September"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "oct_bf_events"] <- "October"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "nov_bf_events"] <- "November"
monthly_bf$propname[monthly_bf$propname == "dec_bf_events"] <- "December"

#Order the months correctly
monthly_bf <- monthly_bf %>%
  arrange(match(propname, month.name))
```

```{r current forecast, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
today <- params$today
date_range <- c(paste0(year(today), "-05-01"), paste0(year(today), "-07-31"))

adj_start <- hydrotools::bf_forecast_start_date(start_date = today,
                                                adjust_start_date = date_range,
                                                gage_data = gage_obj$gage_data,
                                                flow_col = gage_obj$flow_col,
                                                date_col = gage_obj$date_col)

# Determine best AGWRC from rating class
current_forecast_data <- tryCatch(
  expr = {
    gage_obj$baseflow_forecast(start_date = adj_start, AGWRC = list(default = "default"))},
  error = function(e){
    message("No default method defined: ", e$message)
    "No current forecast available."
  }
)    

if (is.character(current_forecast_data) == FALSE){
  percentiles_plot <- gage_obj$plot_percentiles(start_date = adj_start - 30,
                          end_date = max(current_forecast_data$Date)) + 
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = current_forecast_data, 
                     aes(x = Date,
                         y = Forecast,
                         colour = "Current Forecast"), color = "green", linewidth = 2)

current_forecast <- gage_obj$plot_baseflow_forecast(
  start_date = adj_start,
  forecast_days = 0:90,
  AGWRC = list(Constant_AGWRC = "lm_constant",
               Variable_AGWRC = "lm_variable",
               Iterative_AGWRC = params$iterative_AGWRC),
  return_plotly = FALSE,
  include_days_before = 60,
  use_limits = TRUE
)

# create forecast table
short_table <- current_forecast_data |> 
  filter(Day %in% c(15, 30, 45, 90)) |> 
  select(Day, Date, AGWRC, Forecast, obs_flow) |> 
  mutate(percentile = NA)

for (i in 1:nrow(short_table)){
pctile <- ecdf(
  gage_obj$gage_data$value[
    lubridate::month(gage_obj$gage_data$time) == month(short_table$Date[i])
    ]
)

short_table$percentile[i] <- paste0(round(pctile(short_table$Forecast[i]) * 100, 2), "%")
}

current_forecast_table <- flextable(short_table) |> 
  set_header_labels(obs_flow = "Observed",
                    percentile = "Percentile")

} else {
  percentiles_plot <- "Percentile plot not available."
  current_forecast_table <- "Table not available."
}
```

## Overview and Recommended AGWRC

AGWRC analysis for USGS **`r params$gageid`: `r gage_obj$station_name`**. `r cs_conclusion` 

## Terminology

**Regression AGWRC**: the AGWRC calculated by imputing starting flow from manually selected flow event into AGWRC vs Flow Regression

**Event AGWRC**: the AGWRC from a known baseflow event identified by the workflow

**Iterative AGWRC**: the manually selected AGWRC that provides the "best fit" for the manually selected baseflow event

**Starting flow**: the observed flow at the first day of the manually selected baseflow event

**MAE**: Mean Absolute Error

**RMSE**: Root Mean Square Error

**MAPE**: Mean Absolute Percentage Error

## Current Forecast

The current forecast begins at the the lowest flow that occurs between the months of the previous May and July, and extends through today's date. This forecast is based on the assumption that evapotranspiration (ET) occurs at a constant rate of  and that no additional groundwater recharge may occur. As ET decreases in the Fall (usually around late September and early October), it is typical to see a small increase in flow of between 5 – 10%.

## AGWRC Regression Analysis

```{r regression plot, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
tryCatch(
  expr = {
    gage_obj$plot_baseflow_agwrc(CI = TRUE, omsite = omsite, return_plotly = FALSE)

    # R-squared interpretation based on value from database props
    rsqr <- gage_props$propvalue[gage_props$propname == "regression_Rsq"]

    rsqr_interpretation <- interpret_rsqr(rsqr)},
  error = function(e){
    message("Regression analysis unavailable: ", e$message)
    "Regression analysis unavailable."
    rsqr <<- NA
    rsqr_interpretation <<- NA
  })

```

**Figure 2.** AGWRC vs Median Flow Regression. **`r qc_df$propvalue[qc_df$propname == "total_bf_events"]`** baseflow events were identified at USGS 01638500. An AGWRC value was calculated for each event based on the exponential decay of flow during the identified baseflow event. The R-squared value is: `r rsqr`. `r rsqr_interpretation`

## Non-Exceedance Probability Table

Non-Exceedance Probability is the statistical chance that stream flow is recorded at or below a specific value. A 5% NEP of 40 cfs indicates that stream flow will be at or below 40 cfs 5% of the time.

```{r 4 plots w/ patchwork, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = TRUE}
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16)
  )

} else {
  message("Forecast comparison plot skipped: need 4 forecasts, found ", length(forecast_plot))
}
```

## Prediction Accuracy Analysis

Below is a summary of common forecast accuracy metrics that highlight the difference between predicted and actual flow values for each identified baseflow event at USGS `r params$gageid`. Each of these methods emphasize different aspects of error and should be interpreted together. 

### MAE, RMSE, MAPE, Bias, and $R^2$ Analysis 

Both MAE and RMSE are scale-dependent metrics. MAE provides the absolute difference between actual and predicted flow values without indicating relative error size. RMSE provides the square root of the average squared error. Unlike MAE which ignores the magnitude of outliers, RMSE penalizes large errors more heavily. 

MAPE is a scale-independent metric that provides the average absolute error as a percentage of the actual flow value. However, the MAPE calculation fails if the actual flow value is zero and produces unrealistically high values when the actual flow value is close to zero. This can be an issue for small gages that occasionally run dry or approach extreme low-flow condition. MAPE also tends to over-penalize over- and under-forecasting. 

Forecast bias provides an average error where a positive value is indicative of over-forecasting flow and a negative value is indicative of under-forecasting flow. 

The R-squared value, or coefficient of determination, explains the proportion of variance in the actual flow values that is explained by the predicted flow values. This shows how well the model captures any patterns in the data. A value of 1 or -1 suggests a perfect fit while a value of 0 suggests that the model does no better than predicting the mean flow value each time.

**Table 6.** Calculations of the MAE, RMSE, MAPE, Bias, and $R^2$ values for all USGS `r params$gageid` GroupIDs 

```{r error calculations, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
devtools::source_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HARPgroup/baseflow_storage/refs/heads/Emily_bf_workflow/PredictionAccuracyUpdated.R")

flow_csv <- gage_obj$gage_data |>
 select(time, value) |>
 rename(Date = time, Observed = value)

baseflow_csv <- all_data$trimmed_events_df |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) |>
  group_by(GroupID) |>
  mutate(duration = as.numeric(max(Date) - min(Date))) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(duration >= 7) |>
  select(GroupID, Date, Flow, AGWRC, duration)

regression_csv <- all_data$lm_df

m <- regression_csv$m
b <- regression_csv$b

Results <- PredictionAccuracy(flow_csv, baseflow_csv, days = c(0:15), AGWRC = "lm_constant", m, b)

Results$summary_table <- Results$summary_table %>%
  colformat_double(
    j = c("MAPE", "MAE", "RMSE", "Bias", "r2"),
    digits = params$digits
  )
Results$summary_table
```

**Table 7.** All GroupIDs with an MAPE over 20%. These events did not perform well and further analysis with these events should be preceded with caution.

```{r high MAPE, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
filtered_group_stats <- Results$group_stats %>%
  filter(MAPE > 20) %>% 
   mutate(across(c(MAPE, MAE, RMSE, Bias, r2),~round(.x, params$digits)))

flextable(filtered_group_stats) %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  autofit()
```

## Case Studies

Below are recorded case studies conducted by DEQ employees. These case studies are typically done for historical low flow years in Virginia, such as 2023, 2008, 2007, 2002, 1998, and 1966. Additional years may be investigated based on historical low flows at the particular gage of interest. These case studies provide insight into gage behavior at low flow conditions to aid in selecting the most appropriate projection method for making current forecasts. The selected projection method (Variable AGWRC, Constant AGWRC, or BPJ AGWRC) is included on each plot (if applicable), and a brief commentary and analysis is written below each plot.  

```{r case study graph, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = TRUE}
if (is.null(cs_df) || 
    nrow(cs_df) == 0 || 
    ncol(cs_df) == 0 || 
    isTRUE(all(is.na(cs_df)))) {
  message("No case studies for this gage have been saved")
} else {
   cs_plot <- list()

for(i in 1:nrow(cs_df)) {

  cs_sd <- cs_df$startdate[i]

  cs_ed <- cs_df$enddate[i]

  diff_days <- as.numeric(cs_ed - cs_sd)

  BPJ_AGWRC <- as.numeric(cs_df$propcode[i])

  cs_text <- str_wrap(cs_df$proptext[i])

  p_label <- paste0("Interpretation: ", cs_text)
  
  cs_rating_class <- cs_df$propvalue[i]
  
  projection_method <- rating_class_method(cs_rating_class)   
  
  if (is.na(projection_method)) {
  method_label <- "No projection available"
  } else if (projection_method == "lm_variable") {
  method_label <- "Variable AGWRC"
  } else if (projection_method == "lm_constant") {
  method_label <- "Constant AGWRC"
  } else {
  method_label <- paste0("BPJ AGWRC = ", projection_method)
  }
    
  p <- gage_obj$plot_baseflow_forecast(
  start_date = cs_sd,
  forecast_days = 0:diff_days,
  AGWRC = projection_method,
  return_plotly = FALSE,
  include_days_before = 60,
  use_limits = TRUE) +
    labs(caption = cs_text) +
    theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
    scale_color_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    labels = method_label
    )

  cs_plot[[i]] <- p

  print(p)
}
}

```

**Table 9.** Other relevant QC metrics. The Breusch–Pagan test and the White test are statistical methods to quantify heteroscedasticity (when the variability of the dependent variable is not constant). Both tests check for heteroskedasticity; the Breusch–Pagan test assumes normal residuals and detects linear heteroscedasticity while the White test is more general and detects both linear and nonlinear heteroskedasticity. A significant p-value (less than 0.05) suggests sufficient evidence for heteroskedasticity in the flow data. The recorded flow values indicate the gage length, or the total number of non-NA flow values recorded over the entire date range of data collection. The watershed slope is the average slope in the entire drainage basin expressed as a percentage of the vertical rise over the the horizontal distance. 

```{r misc QC metrics, warning = FALSE, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#filter for values of interest
misc_qc <- qc_df %>%
  filter(propname %in% c ("breusch_pagan_p", "white_test_p", "non_na_flow_count"))

#remove unwanted columns
misc_qc <- misc_qc[ , -c(1, 2, 5)]

#add watershed slope as a row
misc_qc_table <- rbind(
  misc_qc[, 1:2],
  c(names(misc_qc)[3], misc_qc[1, 3])
)

#transpose the data into an easier to read format
misc_qc_table_t <- setNames(as.data.frame(t(misc_qc_table$propvalue)), misc_qc_table$propname)


#print table
misc_qc_table_ft <- flextable(misc_qc_table_t) %>% 
  set_header_labels(
    white_test_p = "White Test p-value",
    breusch_pagan_p = "Breush-Pagan p-value",
    non_na_flow_count = "Recorded Flow Values",
    watershed_slope = "Watershed Slope (%)"
  ) %>%
  autofit()

misc_qc_table_ft
```
